doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Chaotic masters and engineer Roger Seibel
summary: Masters often arrived as wrong tapes or copies of copies, so engineer Roger Seibel fixed them, sometimes using records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: That’s really fascinating. And I’ve always wondered, to do those re-issues, did you have access to master tapes or were you doing disc transfers?

You know everything about Sun Ra and Alton Abraham was chaotic. They both died intestate. Okay? You know now all kinds of masters are showing up. I don’t know much about that but we had difficulty obtaining good masters. We had signed contracts for certain recordings that I selected. And then we would get a box of tapes from, you know, UPS, and it wasn’t necessarily what we had contracted for. And sometimes the masters were not the original masters. Sometimes they were copies of copies. And sometimes the things that we had licensed we didn’t get at all. So there were occasions where we went from records. There were. But we didn’t mess around. We had one of the finest engineers doing that stuff working for us, Roger Seibel in Phoenix, Arizona. He was like a magician. Sometimes we had to use records to pull out a part and put it in the tape. Everything was rough. They were not always original masters and it was always a surprise, just like Sun Ra.
